exercise.name: Treadmill Run
library_steps: Step on, clip the safety key to your clothes and start at a walk.
Raise the speed to a pace where you can talk in short sentences.
Slow to a walk for the last few minutes before you stop.
exercise.one_line_summary: Running on a treadmill belt. Picture 1: right foot pushing off behind, left knee driven forward; picture 2: the other leg. Arms swing opposite, elbows ~90 deg.

movement.start: hip ~25 deg behind, knee nearly straight, heel up

muscles.role: Library primary 'cardio' has no mask; front thigh lit (library secondary).

muscles.emg: Hamstrings active late swing and early stance (S1).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Hands on the rails while running.

sources.citation: Novacheck TF. The biomechanics of running. Gait Posture. 1998;7(1):77-95.
sources.what_it_gave: Running kinematics and EMG timing: stance-leg extension at toe-off, swing hip flexion, quadriceps at landing, hamstrings late swing, calves through stance.

sources.citation: Van Hooren B, Fuller JT, Buckley JD, et al. Is motorized treadmill running biomechanically comparable to overground running? A systematic review and meta-analysis of cross-over studies. Sports Med. 2020;50(4):785-813.
sources.what_it_gave: Treadmill running kinematics and muscle activity are largely comparable to overground running.

sources.citation: Meyns P, Bruijn SM, Duysens J. The how and why of arm swing during human walking. Gait Posture. 2013;38(4):555-562.
sources.what_it_gave: Arms swing opposite to the legs in walking and running.

clip_check.check: stance leg: hip / knee at toe-off
clip_check.target: hip ~25 deg behind, knee nearly straight, heel up -> (other leg) (15-35)

clip_check.check: swing leg: thigh forward / knee bend
clip_check.target: thigh ~45 deg forward, knee ~90 deg -> (other leg) (thigh 35-60, knee 70-110)

clip_check.check: Machine parts meet the hands/feet; levers keep their length
clip_check.target: moving rod lengths equal at start and end (+-1 cm)
